units.source_text: 喜撰法师诗云：“庵在京东南，地名宇治山。

en.t: The monk Kisen wrote in a poem: "My hermitage lies southeast of the capital, in a place called Mount Uji.

units.source_text: 人言是忧世，我独居之安。”

en.t: People call it a sorrowful world, but I live here alone in peace."
This appears in the Kokin Wakashu.

units.source_text: “宇治”和“忧世”在日语中发音相同。

en.t: In Japanese, "Uji" and "the sorrowful world" are pronounced alike.
